name: Rewind yourself
summary: On a key, the unit snaps back to where it stood, at the health it had, a few seconds earlier, undoing the damage it took and the ground it covered since; then it waits out a recharge. It is a dive-and-escape tool: run in, do the job, rewind out with the wounds of the raid gone. Unlike a teleport the destination is not chosen, it is wherever the unit was, so an enemy who knows the window can wait there; unlike a heal it also moves the unit, and it never restores more than the unit had a few seconds ago. Some versions also clear debuffs, reload the weapon or make the unit untouchable for the instant of the rewind; one shows an echo at the return spot, one ends with a blast where it lands, and one rewinds only health during a dash to a chosen spot.
counterplay: Burst it down inside the window: a kill before the key is pressed is final, and damage dealt before the window began stays.
Strike while the key recharges: after a rewind it has no second escape for a while.
Freeze, stun or silence it, so it can't press the key at all.
Wait at the spot it will snap back to, which you can work out from where it stood a few seconds ago.
Spread damage out over time instead of front-loading it, so little of it falls inside the window that the rewind undoes.

other_examples.note: An ultimate on a cooldown that sends the hero back to where it stood a few seconds earlier, with the health and mana it had then, while dodging projectiles in flight and removing debuffs. An upgrade lets it target an allied hero as well.

While the ultimate is ready or nearly so, a delayed afterimage trails the champion, marking where he stood a few seconds ago; his team always sees it, enemies only when it is within their sight. On cast he is briefly in stasis, rushes back to the afterimage, heals a set amount plus a share of the health he lost in that time, and sets off a blast where he lands.

A short-cooldown dash to a chosen spot, invulnerable on the way, that heals back all the damage the hero took in the last moment; unlike a full rewind it does not take him back to where he was. An upgrade adds a follow-up that, used within a moment of landing, sends him back to where the dash started, without changing his health again.

shooter_analogues.note: A cooldown ability in a hero shooter: the hero jumps back a few seconds, to her earlier position and the highest health she had in that time, and her weapon is reloaded. She can't be hurt during the brief rewind and most debuffs are cleared. The usual play is to blink in, stick a bomb and recall out; enemies answer by bursting her before she reacts or by hacking her abilities.

player_translation.summary: Press Q and you snap back to where you stood a few seconds ago, with the health you had then. Dive in, do the damage, rewind out; but the key then recharges, and anyone who saw where you came from knows where you will reappear.
as_user: You play aggressively because you have an undo: commit to a dive, plant a charge or take a bad trade, then rewind before it kills you.
Timing is everything: press too early and you lose the gains of the dive, too late and you are already dead.
You think a few seconds ahead: wherever you stand now is your escape route, so you pass through safe spots on your way in.
After a rewind you are exposed until the key comes back, so you play safe for a while.
as_target: The damage you just dealt vanishes, which feels bad, but you know the trick now: finish it in one burst, or wait.
An echo or trail shows where it will return to; turn your guns there.
Watch its cooldown indicator: once it has rewound, the next fight is a fair one.
Freezes, stuns and silences stop the rewind; save them for this unit.
teammates: A rewinder is natural bait: it draws a crowd into the open, then vanishes, leaving them exposed to its team.
Its team knows where it will reappear and can cover that spot.
In the ally variant it rescues a teammate who is about to die, pulling them back a few seconds.
Enemy teams coordinate a disable and a burst on it at the same time.
controls: Q (or R as a second ability): tap to rewind; there is no aiming, since the destination is fixed.
Ally variant: Q with a teammate under the cursor rewinds them instead; double-tap Q rewinds yourself.
Anchor variant: tap Q to drop an anchor at your current spot and health, tap again within a short time to return to it.
feedback: A faint echo or ghost trail behind the unit, visible to everyone while the rewind is ready, marking where it would land.
A rewind effect that plays the unit's path backwards in a flash, then a clear arrival flash; the health bar visibly refills to its old value.
A cooldown ring around the unit's health bar that enemies can read.
A distinct sound on use, loud enough for nearby enemies to hear.
changes_from_rts: Nothing in the RA3 sources marks where Tanya will return; from a top-down camera the enemy needs a visible echo, or the escape feels unfair.
RA3 lets her rewind back several seconds with a short recharge; keep the window short and the recharge clear, so the cost of a wasted rewind is felt.
A rewind must never restore more health than the unit had at the start of the window, and should not restore ammo or charges unless a variant says so.

It interacts with many systems: attached infesters, tethers, burning, objectives and seats; decide each (here: attachments drop off, objectives carried are dropped, the unit can't rewind out of a vehicle seat).
The Time Belt leaves Tanya free to move at once; keep that, but give the arrival a brief flash so enemies can react.

team_play.notes: Mostly a solo survival tool, but it makes the unit strong bait, the ally variant rescues a teammate in trouble, and the enemy team must coordinate a disable and a burst to answer it.

notes: Store a short history of the unit's position and health on the server, a few samples per second, and restore the right one on use.
The return point must be checked: a spot that is now blocked, on a moving platform or inside a closed door needs a fallback to the nearest safe point.
Decide what the rewind clears (debuffs, attachments, burning) and what it keeps (ammo, cooldowns, objectives) in one rule table.
Networking: the rewind is server-side, so clients see a smooth reverse effect rather than a jump; kill credit for damage that was undone needs a rule.
On a dive unit with burst damage it removes most of the risk of diving; the recharge time is the main lever.
A short recharge or a long window makes the unit nearly unkillable for teams without burst or disables.
Combined with heals or shields it can stack into far more effective health than its price allows.
The ally variant can deny kills on high-value teammates again and again.
Damage that disappears is confusing unless the effect is loud and the health bar visibly jumps back.
Without an echo, enemies can't predict the return spot and the counterplay of waiting there vanishes.
In a crowded fight, a unit snapping back across the screen can look like a teleport or a glitch.

variants.name: Full rewind
variants.summary: Position and health snap back to what they were a few seconds earlier; nothing else changes, and the unit can move at once.

variants.name: Clean rewind
variants.summary: The rewind also reloads the weapon and clears most debuffs, and the unit is untouchable for the instant of the rewind.
variants.seen_in: Overwatch Tracer's Recall; Dota 2 Time Lapse removes debuffs

variants.name: Visible echo
variants.summary: While the rewind is ready, a faint delayed image follows the unit, so everyone can see where it would return.
variants.seen_in: League of Legends Ekko's Chronobreak afterimage

variants.name: Rewind while dashing
variants.summary: Only the health rewinds: a quick dash to a spot you choose, untouchable on the way, heals back the damage taken in the last moment. The enemy can no longer camp the return spot, so the window is shorter.

adds_strengths.why: A quick dash to a spot it picks, untouchable on the way, that also heals back the damage it took in the last moment.

adds_weaknesses.why: Only the damage of the last moment is undone, so a slow burst or a kill before the dash still sticks, and the dash then recharges.

variants.name: Set an anchor
variants.summary: Tap once to mark your current spot and health, tap again within a short time to return to them; the anchor is visible to enemies and can be camped.
variants.seen_in: An original twist on the Time Belt, close to Dota 2 Faceless Void's upgraded Time Walk (which can send him back to where the dash started) and to the early, placed use of Overwatch Sombra's Translocator (which saved position only)

variants.name: Arrival blast
variants.summary: The return ends with a burst that damages enemies around the spot where the unit reappears, turning a camped return point into a trap.

variants.name: Rewind a teammate
variants.summary: Cast on a nearby teammate to send them back to their own earlier spot and health; the user can still target itself.
variants.seen_in: Dota 2 Weaver's Time Lapse with its upgrade

adds_strengths.why: Undoes a bad fight: it snaps back to where it stood, at the health it had, a few seconds earlier.
Can pull a dying teammate back to where they stood a few seconds earlier, at the health they had.
Undoes a bad fight: it snaps back to where it stood, at the health it had, a few seconds earlier.

adds_weaknesses.why: Its escape is fixed in advance: it can only go back to where it was, and while the key recharges it has no way out.

counters.why: Chip damage and damage over time taken inside the window are simply wound back.

countered_by.why: Locked out of its abilities, it can't press the key and dies where it stands.
A frozen unit can't use abilities, so freezing it stops the rewind before a teammate breaks it.

open_questions: Should the return point be visible to enemies by default (an echo), or only in a variant? (Recommended: by default, as the counterplay depends on it.)
What does the rewind clear: debuffs, burning, attached infesters, a stasis hold? (Recommended: debuffs and attachments yes; it can't be used while held or frozen.)
Should damage that was undone still count toward kill credit and ultimate charge for the enemy who dealt it?
Is the rewind only for infantry heroes, or can a vehicle or walker carry one too?

shooter_fit.reason: Overwatch's Tracer shows the rewind already works for a player hero; it is cheap to build, gives a dive unit a clear skill ceiling, and has readable counterplay (burst, disable, camp the echo) when the return point is shown.

review.notes: Re-checked field by field against its sources by the batch r1 checker, which covered all 33 batch patterns; research/r1/checker/checks.json lists every field and verdict. Nothing was found wrong.
